_comment: Golden test cases for the file-loading pipeline. Expected values are hand-checked,
not merely recorded: the fixture generator (scripts/make_test_fixtures.py) decides
how many data rows each sheet gets, and the numbers below are those counts.
Each case drives two levels of assertion (see tests/loading_checks.py):
tables  - DataLoader.tables() keys and each frame's [rows, columns]
origins - DataLoader.origins, mapping a table name back to its uploaded file
inspect - workbook_probe.inspect_file, one entry per file in `files` order
Table naming is not incidental. A workbook contributing one surviving sheet is
keyed by its bare filename; two or more surviving sheets are keyed
'<sheet> (<stem>)<ext>' (data_loader.py:69). Cases below assert both branches.
Every case is duplicated across .xlsx and .xls because the two are read by
different libraries (openpyxl vs xlrd) sharing only workbook_probe._extent.
Optional per-case fields and their defaults:
selections     - dict passed to DataLoader.add_files / JSON-encoded into
the API's `selections` form field. null means no
preference, which the pipeline reads as 'every sheet'.
selections_raw - a literal string sent as the form field instead, for the
malformed-payload cases that cannot be expressed as JSON.
levels         - which suites run the case; defaults to both.
['api'] for cases that only exist at the HTTP boundary.
inspect        - null means 'not asserted here', used where another case
already pins the same file's probe output.
rows_agree     - whether workbook_probe's total row count must equal the
rows DataLoader actually loaded. Defaults to true when
`selections` is null and false otherwise: a narrowed
selection loads fewer rows than the workbook holds, so
the two legitimately diverge (9 vs 6 for a 2-of-3
subset). Only meaningful on cases expecting status 200.
Fields added for the hazard, encoding and failure-mode groups:
columns        - table name -> expected column names, asserted where the
headers are the point (whitespace stripping, numeric and
blank headers, non-ASCII).
loader_raises  - exception class name DataLoader.add_files is expected to
raise at unit level. Only on failure-mode cases.
has_error      - on an inspect entry, asserts an `error` key is present
without pinning its wording.
optional       - the fixture is not committed (see scale-50k-rows); the
case is skipped rather than failed when it is absent.
xfail          - `expect` records the CORRECT behaviour, which the current
code does NOT produce. The case is expected to fail; when
someone fixes the defect it starts passing unexpectedly,
which is the signal to drop the flag. Every xfail case
carries a `known_issue` explaining the defect and the fix.
known_issue    - prose description of a confirmed defect. Two exist today,
both rooted in _read_csv_with_encoding being unable to
fail: latin-1 shadows cp1252, and a corrupt workbook is
silently reported as a readable CSV.

rows 5-14 carry a fill but no values, so the sheet's dimension reports 14 rows while only 3 hold data. This is the exact failure workbook_probe's docstring exists to prevent: the probe's row count must equal what DataLoader loads, or the UI promises rows the analysis never delivers. (.xlsx only - in .xls the count comes from xlrd's own row view, and an xlwt-built fixture would be testing xlwt's idea of a used range rather than Excel's.)
plain utf-8, the first rung of the ladder
utf-8 with a BOM - pandas strips it, so the first column is 'id' and not '\ufeffid'
utf-16, reached when the utf-8 attempt raises UnicodeDecodeError

a cp1252 file using characters that exist in cp1252 but NOT in latin-1 (U+2019 and U+20AC sit at bytes 0x92 and 0x80, which are control codes in latin-1). Records the CORRECT expectation, which current code does not meet - see known_issue.
cases.known_issue: The encoding ladder at data_loader.py:75 is ['utf-8', 'utf-16', 'latin-1', 'iso-8859-1', 'cp1252'], tried in order. latin-1 and iso-8859-1 decode ANY byte sequence without raising, so cp1252 is unreachable - it is dead code at the end of the list. This file decodes as latin-1 and its headers come back as 'pr\x92ce' and 'cost\x80' instead of 'pr\u2019ce' and 'cost\u20ac'. Fix: try cp1252 before latin-1, since cp1252 is the stricter superset and does raise on its five undefined bytes.

cases.description: a zero-byte upload. /api/inspect reports it per-file and keeps going so one bad file does not sink the batch; /api/analyze-full rejects the whole request at the size check (api.py:316) before any loading happens.

a real CSV wearing an .xlsx extension. pd.read_excel raises ValueError and DataLoader falls back to a CSV read (data_loader.py:40), so the upload succeeds rather than failing on a wrong extension the user cannot see.

a valid workbook cut off mid-archive. Records the CORRECT expectation - the probe should report it unreadable and the API should refuse it with a 4xx - which current code does not meet. See known_issue.
cases.known_issue: The probe and the loader disagree on corrupt workbooks, and the disagreement is user-visible. workbook_probe.inspect_file catches the BadZipFile with `except Exception` and falls back to a CSV read, which SUCCEEDS on the binary remains - so /api/inspect reports kind='csv', rows=3, no error. DataLoader._add_excel catches only ValueError, and zipfile.BadZipFile is not one, so the same file raises there and /api/analyze-full returns a generic 502. The UI therefore promises a readable 3-row table and the analysis then dies. Two things are wrong: the CSV fallback cannot fail (see enc-cp1252-specific-chars for the same root cause), and the two code paths catch different exception sets.

cases.description: 50,000 rows x 12 columns: asserts the pipeline loads a large workbook and that the probe's count still matches what pandas loads at scale. Not committed - build it with `python scripts/make_test_fixtures.py --scale`. BIFF8 caps at 65,536 rows / 256 columns, so there is no .xls counterpart.
